To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TLRs control dendritic cell functions in distinct anatomical sites to orchestrate adaptive immune responses.
TLRs are important regulators of dendritic cell function and that they control the development of adaptive immune responses.
Toll like receptors control adaptive immune responses through dendritic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control innate immunity and adaptive immunity.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that control the innate and adaptive immune responses in the context of microbial infection.
the mechanisms that control the activation of dendritic cells and the initiation of adaptive responses to pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TLR mediated signals control the initiation of adaptive immunity by regulating multiple aspects of dendritic cell functions.
TLRs control the adaptive immune responses by orchestrating the innate immune responses that provide a permissive environment for the activation of antigen specific T and B cell responses.
TLRs are a key component of innate immune system that initiate and control the activation of adaptive immune responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TLRs are key regulators of adaptive immunity.
TLRs control the initiation of innate immunity, and in turn, TLRs also control the initiation of the adaptive immune response.
dendritic cells sense pathogens via TLRs, process and present pathogen associated molecular patterns, and activate the adaptive immune system to eliminate the invading microorganisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TLR signaling pathways are critically involved in controlling the development of adaptive immunity.
TLR mediated control is critical for the initiation of adaptive immunity and is a major determinant of the nature and the quality of the adaptive responses that are generated.
TLRs are critical for the development of protective adaptive immunity against pathogens.
